backward_compat_traps.rule: SPMI/RFFE use SCLK/SDATA + SSC + Bus Park, not SDA/SCL + START/STOP.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Treating the bus as I2C (open-drain, 7-bit address, START/STOP) breaks framing and addressing.
Expecting separate MOSI/MISO or a chip-select pin fails — slaves are selected by 4-bit ID in the command frame.

backward_compat_traps.rule: Every frame carries an odd parity bit.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Omitting or mis-computing parity makes the receiver ignore the frame.

backward_compat_traps.rule: Register 0 Write carries 7 data bits in the command frame (single-frame).
backward_compat_traps.trap: Treating Register 0 Write like a normal Register Write adds spurious frames.

backward_compat_traps.rule: RFFE has one master; SPMI is multi-master with arbitration.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Implementing RFFE arbitration (or omitting SPMI arbitration) is wrong for the respective bus.

fields.spec_version: MIPI System Power Management Interface (SPMI) v2.0 + RF Front-End Control Interface (RFFE) v3.0 (MIPI Alliance)
previous_versions: SPMI v1.0 — initial multi-master two-wire system-power-management bus; Register Read/Write, Extended Register, Register 0 Write.
RFFE v1.0 / v2.0 — single-master RF-front-end control bus; Register Write/Read, Extended Register, Register 0 Write; up to 26 MHz.

key_changes.summary: Extended multi-master arbitration, the Device Descriptor Block, Authenticated commands, Master Read/Write, and the Reset/Sleep/Shutdown/Wakeup power-state command set; the two-wire SCLK/SDATA + SSC + parity + 4-bit-ID model is carried forward.
Added Extended Register Long, Masked Write, Mapped Register Write, the Trigger/Timed mechanism, Group (GSID) commands, and raised the maximum clock to 52 MHz; the two-wire framing model is unchanged.

fields.version_naming_history_note: SPMI and RFFE are maintained by the MIPI Alliance. They share a two-wire SCLK/SDATA control-bus model (SSC framing, per-frame parity, 4-bit IDs) and are specified here as one combined control-bus class. Facts here are grounded in the public MIPI SPMI and RFFE specifications.
